summary: Toru Haneda (1882–1955) was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1907) and held a post at Kyoto University from circa 1909 to 1945.
Toru Kumeji works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Center for Open Humanities Data and at the Humanities Information Studies Institute, where he was attested as chief researcher in 2015.

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, and founded the Koreanology Association. He served as professor at Keijo Imperial University (~1926–1945) and Tenri University (~1950–1965), and also held a post at Fukuoka University.

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne. He held posts at Lausanne (attested 1998), the Humanities Information Studies Institute, and the Center for Open Humanities Data.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (-1982) under scholars including Karl Hoffmann. He served as a professor at Osaka University and at Tohoku University (attested 2003–2012).
Toshihide Mori is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held an appointment as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies, studying at Keio University (~1931–1937) and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Keio (~1937–1969), McGill University (~1969–1975), and Komazawa University (attested 1988).

Toshihiko Kimura is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He later taught part-time at Tohoku, and held posts at Tokai Gakuin University (attested 1981–1987) and Shitennoji University (attested 2015).

Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as an associate professor and held an academic post at Nagoya University from circa 1989 to 2019.

Toshiichi Endo specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (-1995) under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake, later becoming a professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Toshikazu Watanabe specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011), the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2015–2019), and Kokugakuin University (2018).

Toshiki Osada is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Hokkaido University. He held positions at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature as professor and project leader (~2003–2018) and at Kyoto University of the Arts.

Toshinori Ochiai is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He served at Kacho Junior College, as professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2018), and as director of the Research Institute of Old Japanese Manuscripts.
Toshio Ando (1909–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1928 to 1931. He held academic posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1955–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2008). He completed a postdoctoral post at Zhejiang University (~2018) and visited Toyo University's Institute of Oriental Studies.

Toshio Nagahiro (1905–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1926–1929), he served there as professor (~1956–1969) and later held a post at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1969–1980).

Toshio Sako is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University with doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Hannan University, the University of Tokyo (~1955–1977), and Chuo University (~1977–1987).

Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor of Indian studies at Nagoya University's Graduate School of Letters (attested 2009).
Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Seiran Ouchi and Enryo Inoue. He held a post at Nihon University.
